title: Private/on‑prem Activation Lifecycle & Sprint Catalog — Q2 Operational Readiness
creator: Aisha Morgan
description:
Purpose: Define a sprintable catalog of activation workstreams, acceptance gates, and linked runbooks to reduce time-to-first-successful-private-deployment by 40% for Q2. Scope covers VPC & air-gapped on‑prem installs, third-party KMS integration patterns, upgrade/rollback safe paths, canary automation for initial customer cohorts, and a compact checklist for Solutions Engineering handoffs.

Why this ticket: Customers onboarding private instances today experience unpredictable lead times driven by bespoke infra checks (KMS compatibility, NFS mount stability, network egress rules) and manual cutovers. We need a repeatable operational path that productizes the common checks as discrete sprint tasks and maps them to OKRs and SLOs so PM/Eng/SE can reliably commit to dates.

Deliverables: 1) Sprint catalog of 10 activation tasks with owners and test criteria; 2) Canary automation playbook for cohort rollouts (scripts + dashboard alerts); 3) KMS compatibility matrix and integration checklist for common vendors (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Vault HSM patterns); 4) Upgrade & rollback runbook templates; 5) Go/no-go acceptance criteria aligned to OKR metric targets.

Success metrics: 1) Private onboarding mean lead time reduced 40% vs baseline (baseline: 18 business days); 2) First-time activation success rate >= 90% for three pilot customers; 3) Canary rollback automation triggers and completes within SLO (15m) in >= 95% of simulated failures.

Stakeholders: Product Management (PM), Solutions Engineering, Release Engineering, Security/Compliance, Customer Success, and Legal for contracts affecting data residency.
comments: 2026-02-24 — Kickoff meeting: aligned on scope and lead metrics. Decided to limit initial vendor-specific KMS integrations to AWS KMS and HashiCorp Vault to reduce scope risk.
2026-03-02 — SE input: common failure modes from recent onboardings documented in Confluence; recommended adding an NFS health-check and registry certificate validation step to the sprint catalog.

2026-03-07 — Eng prioritization call: ENG-2401 (canary orchestration) needs API contract freeze before automation work begins; added dependency. Eng proposed a multi-stage canary (internal -> pilot customer -> broader rollout).
2026-03-11 — Security review triage: preliminary checklist reviewed, full security review required for KMS and HSM patterns; delaying secret rotation automation to Q3 to avoid scope slippage.

2026-03-14 — PM decision: split catalog into two waves (Wave A: essential activation checks + canary automation; Wave B: extended integrations and post-activation telemetry). Assigned Wave A lead: Liam Chen.
acceptance_criteria: Sprint catalog created and published to Confluence with owners, per-task test steps, and estimated dev effort for each task.
Canary automation scripts checked into github.com/redwood-inference/private-canary repo with CI that runs simulated failure scenarios.
KMS compatibility matrix published and validated against two pilot customers (one AWS-native, one Vault-onprem).
Upgrade/rollback runbook templates reviewed with Release Eng and Solutions Eng and stored in runbooks/private-activation directory.
Dashboard (Console) tile for activation progress and canary health is available in staging and wired to alerting (pagerduty channel: #private-activations).
risk_register: KMS vendor edge cases: vendor misconfiguration at customer sites could extend onboarding time; mitigation: require pre-check script run by SE before scheduling handover.

Network egress/firewall issues: unpredictable infra delays when customers have restrictive networking; mitigation: include a network checklist and sample firewall rules in the catalog and require network readiness signoff.

Canary automation reliability: false positives in failure detection could cause unnecessary rollbacks; mitigation: implement a two-stage confirmation (metric threshold + health-check probe) before triggering rollback.
Resource constraints on Eng: ENG-2401 backlog may delay automation; mitigation: cross-train one SE as a temporary automation owner for initial pilot.
